key_insight: Healthcare staff often assume machine translation will safely handle clinical abbreviations, but the study suggests this trust can mask meaningful patient-safety risk.
clinical_relevance: Using general-purpose MT like Google Translate for patient records or clinical communication may misrender abbreviations, so human oversight is important in higher-stakes healthcare settings.
method: 21 UK healthcare staff were interviewed in semi-structured sessions.
Participants reviewed contextualized French and Spanish examples containing medical abbreviations.
Examples were drawn from authoritative clinical corpora and translated with Google Translate, then analyzed qualitatively and by cross-analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports qualitative analysis of staff responses to GT-translated abbreviation examples, highlighting awareness gaps rather than accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Because the study uses a small interview sample and abbreviation-focused examples, results may not generalize to all clinical MT use cases or languages.
paper_title: "I just assumed that it would translate": examining MT risk awareness among healthcare staff with abbreviations as a use case
